## Dataset A - Slither Audited Smart Contracts (training, validation, in-distribution test)
| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Source | huggingface.co/datasets/mwritescode/slither-audited-smart-contracts (raw shards `data/raw/contracts0-8.parquet`, `big-splits.csv`, `small-splits.csv`, `label_mappings.json`) |
| Creator / citation | Rossini, M. (2022). *Slither Audited Smart Contracts Dataset*. University of Bologna course project. |
| How it was built | Verified Ethereum contracts from Smart Contract Sanctuary / Etherscan, flattened with the Slither flattener and analysed with Slither (38 detector classes). |
| Licence | MIT for the repository; every contract keeps its original licence. Used for non-commercial academic research. |
| Fields used | `source_code` (input) and the raw Slither detector list (target). `bytecode` is not downloaded: the app accepts source code. |
| Target | Multi-label: 7 weakness families (access-control, arithmetic, bad-randomness, locked-ether, other, reentrancy, unchecked-calls); "no flagged weakness" = all classes negative. See `docs/label_decision.md`. |
| Contracts | 120,608 rows -> 120,510 after filtering -> **65,058 unique** after exact de-duplication |

### Preprocessing
1. Line-preserving comment removal (`clean_source`): comments become spaces, every newline is kept.
2. Literal normalisation: strings -> `<STR>`, numbers / hex -> `<NUM>`. User identifiers are **kept** for the
   model (identifier normalisation is evaluated as ablation E4 and used for de-duplication).
3. Regular-expression tokeniser that keeps keywords, operators, identifiers and composite globals such as
   `msg.sender`, `tx.origin`, `block.timestamp` as single tokens.
4. Long-file policy: at most 20,000 tokens; longer files keep the first
   25 % and the last part of the budget (the main contract of a
   flattened file sits at the end). **367 contracts (0.6%) are affected**; the app warns
   when it truncates.
5. Exact and near-duplicate grouping and a group-aware 70/15/15 split (`docs/dedup_report.md`).
6. TF-IDF over token 1-3-grams, vocabulary of 20,000 n-grams chosen on a seeded
   subset of 20,000 *training* contracts (min_df 5,
   max_df 0.95); IDF fitted on the full training split; SVD-512
   (80.4% of variance) also fitted on training data only.
   Transforming one contract takes 4 ms.

## Dataset B - SmartBugs Curated (external gold test only)
| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| Source | github.com/smartbugs/smartbugs-curated, pinned at commit `230e649` (16 Jun 2024) |
| Licence | Apache-2.0 for the repository; each contract keeps its original licence |
| Our counts | 143 contracts, 207 annotated vulnerabilities, 222 distinct annotated lines (the literature quotes about 143 / 208) |
| ICSE 2020 subset | `ICSE2020_curated_69.txt` lists 68 unique paths (all present) |
| Role | Testing only; never used for training, tuning or threshold selection. Note: 42 of the 143 contracts also occur (exactly or nearly) in Dataset A, found after the freeze (`reports/tables/gold_overlap.csv`); results are reported with and without them |
| Leakage control | All comments are removed before any model sees a contract; the build fails if `@vulnerable_at_lines`, `<yes>` or `<report>` survive (acceptance test A1). 206 of 222 annotated lines carry a `<yes> <report>` marker on the line above; the other 16 belong to multi-line annotations whose marker sits a few lines higher. |

## Limitations and threats to validity
* **Weak labels.** Targets are Slither findings, not expert judgements; in-distribution scores measure agreement
  with Slither. SmartBugs (human annotations) is the independent check.
* **Clone leakage.** 46.0% of contracts are exact (renamed) duplicates and many
  more are near-duplicates; a random split would put 58.5% of validation and test
  contracts next to a clone in training. Measured explicitly in experiment E2.
* **Giant template families.** Clone groups larger than 1 % of the pool always go to training
  (6 groups, 10,085 contracts), so they are never evaluated.
* **Label conflicts.** 56 groups of identical (normalised) code carry
  different Slither labels - a direct measure of label noise (e.g. different compiler versions).
* **Domain shift.** SmartBugs is 99.3% Solidity 0.4 and its median
  contract is 127 tokens; the training pool is 21.8% Solidity 0.4 with a
  median of 2,467 tokens.
* **Classes without a counterpart.** SmartBugs Arithmetic (overflow), Denial of Service, Front Running, Time
  Manipulation and Short Addresses cannot be evaluated: no training label exists.
* **SmartBugs has no clean contracts**, so only recall is measured there; false-positive rates come from the
  held-out test split.
* **Licences.** Contracts keep their original licences; both datasets are cited.
